sources.entry: OpenDictation - Open-source dictation utility with local and cloud speech-to-text. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/kdcokenny/OpenDictation) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Open Dictation is a native macOS dictation utility for Apple silicon Macs that records from a chosen microphone, transcribes the recording with local or cloud speech-to-text, and pastes the result at the cursor.
summary.what_it_does: The app records audio from a selected microphone, transcribes the finished recording, and pastes the text where the cursor is. Whisper runs locally and is the default engine, with optional local Parakeet TDT v2 (English) and v3 (25 European languages) models run through FluidAudio 0.15.6. Cloud presets cover OpenAI GPT Transcribe, GPT-4o mini Transcribe, OpenAI Whisper, and Groq Whisper Turbo, and a custom OpenAI-compatible base URL and model name can be set. A global shortcut (default Option + Space) supports toggle and hold-to-talk modes, and Escape cancels a dictation. A personal dictionary provides recognition hints and literal replacements, and transcript cleanup removes speech-to-text control markers with optional filler-word removal. On supported MacBooks a notch panel shows state; other Macs use audio feedback.
use_cases: dictate text into any app with a keyboard shortcut
transcribe voice notes on a Mac without sending audio to the cloud
use OpenAI or Groq speech-to-text from the menu bar
dictate in European languages with Parakeet models
add custom vocabulary hints for names and jargon in transcription
how_to_run: Download the latest DMG from the project's releases.
For an unsigned build, run: xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine /Applications/OpenDictation.app
Launch the app and grant Microphone and Accessibility permissions.
Open Settings to choose microphone, shortcut, activation mode, engine, or cloud service.
notable: Whisper is the local default, with optional Parakeet models that download only when the user chooses to.
Pastes at the cursor and restores the previous clipboard contents; without Accessibility access the transcript stays on the clipboard.
Microphone selection uses stable Core Audio device IDs and stops with an error if the chosen device is missing rather than switching inputs.
Transcript cleanup is deliberately narrow, avoiding broad punctuation rewrites.
Notch panel shows recording and transcription state on supported MacBooks.
caveats: Requires macOS 14 Sonoma or later and an Apple silicon Mac.
Unsigned builds need a quarantine-removal command before they will launch.
Automatic paste depends on granting Accessibility permission.
